options.game: The Legend of Zelda: Breath of the Wild
options.how: After the plateau tutorial you can go anywhere, tackle shrines and Divine Beasts in any order, or walk straight to Hyrule Castle and fight Ganon.
Thirteen chapters played in a fixed order, each a continuous authored path from City 17 to the Citadel with no map or backtracking.

sources.note: Breath of the Wild: open-air design, go anywhere and tackle challenges in any order
Breath of the Wild: you can head almost directly to Calamity Ganon
Half-Life 2: 13 chapters in sequence
Half-Life 2: storyline chapter by chapter

options.how: One continuous world around Firelink Shrine; elevators and unlocked doors loop areas back on each other, and there is no early fast travel.
The Normandy is the hub: talk to crew, then pick recruitment, loyalty and story missions from the galaxy map, each played as a separate level.

sources.note: Dark Souls: Firelink Shrine hub and elevator shortcuts
Dark Souls: Undead Parish lift opens a permanent shortcut to Firelink
Mass Effect 2: Normandy SR-2 CIC galaxy map used to choose destinations
Mass Effect 2: Normandy as hub between missions

options.how: Each of eight worlds is an overworld map of discrete levels, fortresses and bonus huts; you pick a path between nodes and replay nothing you skip.
Zebes is one map of rooms joined by doors and elevators; new beams and items open earlier dead ends, so you loop back through old areas.

sources.note: Super Mario Bros. 3: world map lets the player choose path and level
Super Metroid: interconnected map design and ability-gated routes

options.how: Peach's Castle is a 3D hub: jump into paintings to enter courses, pick a star mission, and open star-locked doors to reach more paintings.
Nibel is one seamless map without loading screens; abilities like Bash and Double Jump unlock routes in regions you already crossed.
Chapters are grids of short levels picked from a map screen; clear enough of them to reach the chapter boss and unlock the next chapter.

sources.note: Super Mario 64: castle hub with paintings leading to courses
Super Mario 64: mission select and star doors
Ori and the Blind Forest: interconnected Metroidvania map gated by abilities
Super Meat Boy: 300+ levels across chapters

options.how: A condensed Britain you free-roam between events; races, stunts and barn finds are scattered on the map and you drive to them.
48 separate tracks grouped into 12 four-race cups; you pick a cup or a track from a menu and each race loads on its own.
Every ranked match is played in a standard arena with identical dimensions and boost pads; only the cosmetics of the stadium change.

sources.note: Forza Horizon 4: open world condensing Britain
Mario Kart 8 Deluxe: 48 courses in 12 cups
Rocket League: online arenas standardized to the same dimensions

options.how: Numbered chapters each send Isaac to one deck of the Ishimura by tram; a locator line points to the next objective in a set order.
Talos I is one station of linked areas with shortcuts, alternate entries and a spacewalk exterior; side quests send you back through old sections.

sources.note: Dead Space: chapter-based progression through the Ishimura
Dead Space: decks reached by the tram system
Prey: backtracking, shortcuts and alternate paths on Talos I
Prey: exterior spacewalk reveals how areas connect

options.how: Astera is the hub for eating, crafting and taking quests from boards; each hunt deploys you to a separate locale and returns you after.
Missions are self-contained sandboxes (Paris, Sapienza, Marrakesh) picked from a menu and replayed with new starts, disguises and targets.

sources.note: Monster Hunter: World: Astera as the base of operations
Monster Hunter: World: quest counters and departing on expeditions
Hitman: self-contained sandbox missions built for replay
Hitman: mission locations list

options.how: Hallownest is one fixed, hand-drawn map; every room, secret wall and shortcut sits where the designers put it, the same for every player.
Terrain, caves and biomes are generated from a seed as you explore, out to about 30 million blocks in each direction.
Each run lays out levels at random so routes change every time, but from rooms built out of designer-made templates, keeping them playable.

sources.note: Hollow Knight: hand-crafted, vast interconnected world
Minecraft: terrain procedurally generated from a seed
Minecraft: terrain generates to about 30 million blocks
Spelunky: randomized levels each time you play

options.how: The 16 dungeon levels under Tristram's cathedral are regenerated for each new game, so layouts, monsters and loot placement change.
Every Sword Coast area is a fixed, hand-painted isometric map with placed NPCs, quests and encounters, identical on every playthrough.

sources.note: Diablo: ever-changing labyrinth, procedural generation
Baldur's Gate: isometric Sword Coast adventure

note: Baldur's Gate handcrafted areas not confirmed by a cited source in this session

options.how: Each new world is randomly generated: biomes, caverns, ore and dungeons are placed by the generator, so every save digs a different map.

options.game: Ori and the Will of the Wisps
options.how: Niwen is a fixed, hand-painted map where every platform, ability gate and secret is placed by designers for precise traversal.

sources.note: Terraria: randomly generated worlds
Ori and the Will of the Wisps: vast world in hand-painted artwork

options.how: Every mission drops the team into a procedurally generated cave system, so no two missions share a layout.
One fixed island with 500+ puzzles; sightlines and landmarks are placed by hand because the environment itself hides puzzle answers.

sources.note: Deep Rock Galactic: procedurally generated caves, no two missions alike
The Witness: an island with over 500 puzzles to explore

options.how: Thousands of towns and dungeons sit at fixed spots, but wilderness, many dungeon layouts and smaller details are generated by algorithm.
A handcrafted solar system: each planet is built by hand around clues and events that happen at set times, identical for every player.

sources.note: Daggerfall: locations pre-generated, smaller details randomly generated
Daggerfall: size of the generated Iliac Bay
Outer Wilds: explore a handcrafted solar system

options.how: The castle is procedurally generated anew for every heir, so room order and layout change after each death.
The island's biome order and links are fixed by hand; each biome is filled at random from hand-designed room tiles.
A large, labyrinthine world laid out by hand, room by room, with secrets and glitch walls in the same place every game.

sources.note: Rogue Legacy: procedurally generated, new castles with every life
Dead Cells: fixed world layout plus hand-designed tiles assembled by algorithm
Axiom Verge: a large, labyrinthine world

options.how: A procedurally generated universe of planets at galactic scale; you fly between systems and land anywhere on each world.
One small handcrafted island park, crossable in minutes, with trails, secrets and characters packed around a single summit.

sources.note: No Man's Sky: infinite procedurally generated universe full of planets
A Short Hike: explore the island your way on the way to the summit

options.how: Two dense city districts in Tokyo and Osaka crammed with discos, hostess clubs, SEGA arcades and 100 side stories.
A 1:1 scale Milky Way of about 400 billion star systems rendered at true galactic scale, crossed by hyperspace jumps.

sources.note: Yakuza 0: neon-lit Tokyo and Osaka districts with tons of distractions and 100 stories
Elite Dangerous: 1:1 scale galaxy of 400 billion star systems

options.how: One village of back gardens, high street shops and a green, each a small stage dense with people and props to prank.
The whole Earth from map data, with over 1.5 billion buildings; you can take off and fly anywhere on the planet.

sources.note: Untitled Goose Game: from back gardens to high street shops to the village green
Microsoft Flight Simulator: our planet with 1.5 billion buildings

options.how: Each kingdom is a small sandbox packed with Power Moons (93 in the Sand Kingdom), always more than you need to move on.
The Iliac Bay is a generated landmass larger than England, holding thousands of towns and dungeons between long wilderness stretches.

sources.note: Super Mario Odyssey: kingdoms with 9 to 93 Power Moons each
Daggerfall: landmass about 1.685 times the size of England

options.how: Every block mined or placed is saved into the world file, so builds, tunnels and farms stay exactly as players left them.
Every Battle Royale match starts on a fresh island; everything built or destroyed vanishes when the match ends.

sources.note: Minecraft: generated world that players reshape
Fortnite: Battle Royale matches

options.game: The Legend of Zelda: Majora's Mask
options.how: Playing the Song of Time returns Termina to dawn of the first day; NPC progress and most items reset, only masks, songs and key gear stay.
The generated world keeps its history: civilizations rise and fall, and later forts or adventurers explore what earlier play left behind.

sources.note: Majora's Mask: Song of Time warps back to the start of the First Day
Dwarf Fortress: generated rise and fall of civilizations in a simulated world

options.how: The solar system is trapped in a time loop; each loop restores every planet to its start, and only the player's knowledge carries over.
Terraforming, paths, furniture and buildings stay on the island between sessions, so the island grows into the player's design.

sources.note: Outer Wilds: a solar system trapped in an endless time loop
Animal Crossing: New Horizons: terraform to make dramatic changes to your island

options.how: When an heir dies, the castle is procedurally regenerated and the next heir starts the run in a new layout.
Buildings you demolish stay destroyed across the open map, permanently changing routes, cover and the fight for each sector.

sources.note: Rogue Legacy: new castles with every life, your child succeeds you
Red Faction: Guerrilla: permanently modify the game environment

options.how: Every level is built from fully destructible voxels; you plan heists by smashing, blasting or driving through walls to make shortcuts.

options.game: The Last of Us Part I
options.how: Detailed but static environments; routes, cover and stealth paths are authored, and only set pieces like doors or glass change.

sources.note: Teardown: fully destructible voxel environments, anything can be broken
The Last of Us Part I: authored environments and story

options.game: The Legend of Zelda: Majora's Mask
options.how: A 72-hour cycle (about 54 real minutes) with NPC schedules; the moon falls at the end unless you rewind to the first day.
Runs on the console's real clock and calendar: shops close at night, critters change by season and time, holidays fall on real dates.

sources.note: Majora's Mask: three-day cycle reset by the Song of Time
Majora's Mask: moon crashes at the end of the third day
Animal Crossing: New Horizons: critters depend on season and time of day

options.how: A cartridge clock tracks real time: morning, day and night change which wild Pokemon appear, and some NPCs show up on set weekdays.
An in-game day-night cycle flips the loop: scavenge by day, and at sundown fast Volatiles hunt you, turning hunter into hunted.

sources.note: Pokemon Gold and Silver: real-time clock, morning/day/night periods affect encounters
Pokemon Gold and Silver: NPCs appear on certain days of the week
Dying Light: shift from hunter to hunted at sundown

options.how: Civilizations and campaigns drawn from 1,000 years of real history; units, buildings and tech trees follow real cultures.
Greek, Norse and Egyptian pantheons: pick gods for god powers and recruit myth units like Cyclops, Trolls and Mummies.

sources.note: Age of Empires II: 1,000 years of human history, 45+ civilizations
Age of Mythology: Greek, Norse, Egyptian pantheons, god powers and myth units

options.how: A space beetle on an endless track through a hellish void; no literal place, so art and threat are pure shape, light and beat.
Haunted houses and buildings investigated with real ghost-hunting tools (EMF readers, spirit boxes) while the ghost stalks the team.
Survivors live in Moscow's metro stations after an apocalypse left a poisonous surface, so gas masks and scarce ammo shape play.

sources.note: Thumper: rhythm violence, a space beetle braving the hellish void
Phasmophobia: haunted locations and ghost-hunting equipment
Metro 2033: survivors in the Moscow underground, poisonous surface wasteland

options.how: Present-day Los Santos and Blaine County: cars, phones, stock market and satire of current life drive missions and systems.
Captain a spaceship across a generated galaxy; shields, FTL drives, oxygen and teleporting boarders are the core systems.
The Forgotten Realms' Sword Coast under AD&D 2nd Edition rules: spell memorization, magic items and monsters come from D&D.

sources.note: Grand Theft Auto V: the world of Los Santos and Blaine County
FTL: running a spaceship in a randomly generated galaxy
Baldur's Gate: Dungeons and Dragons, Sword Coast, 2nd Edition AD&D rules

options.how: You play Amaterasu, the Japanese sun goddess as a white wolf, fighting the eight-headed Orochi in a Nippon drawn from Shinto myth.
15th-century Florence and Venice rebuilt as playable cities, with real families and Leonardo da Vinci as an ally.
Wireframe shapes and colors pulse to a techno soundtrack; the setting is a synesthetic network, not a literal place.

sources.note: Okami: Amaterasu, the Japanese sun goddess, versus an eight-headed demon
Assassin's Creed II: Florence, Venice and Leonardo da Vinci
Rez: synesthesia, visuals synced to a techno soundtrack, playable in VR

options.how: Soft walls, floors and hatches can be shot or blown open to make new sightlines; defenders reinforce walls and attackers breach them.
Maps never change during a match; walls, angles and grenade spots are fixed, so mastery is memorizing the same geometry.

sources.note: Rainbow Six Siege: shatter walls to create new lines of sight, reinforce walls
Rainbow Six Siege: destruction and reinforced walls
Counter-Strike: Global Offensive: standard maps are indestructible, a mod adds destruction

options.how: Destruction 2.0: chip away cover, blow holes in walls and collapse whole buildings once enough damage is dealt.
Compact multiplayer maps with fixed walls and cover; routes and sightlines stay the same so spawns and lanes can be tuned tightly.

sources.note: Battlefield: Bad Company 2: Destruction 2.0, buildings collapse after enough damage
Call of Duty 4: Modern Warfare: multiplayer maps

note: Call of Duty 4 static maps not confirmed by a cited source in this session

options.how: Physics-based destruction of buildings: knock out a staircase to stop pursuers or drive through blown-out walls.
Fixed waist-high cover arranged by designers defines every fight; the arena layout is a known, stable puzzle of flanks and angles.

sources.note: Red Faction: Guerrilla: fully-dynamic physics-based destruction
Gears of War: cover-based shooter

note: Gears of War static cover not confirmed by a cited source in this session

options.how: Every pixel is simulated: burn, explode or melt the terrain itself, so spells can dig new routes or bury you.
Each floor plan is fixed and walls stay put, so players choreograph a route through set rooms, doors and patrols where one shot kills.

sources.note: Noita: every pixel is simulated, burn, explode or melt anything
Hotline Miami: choreograph your way through situations where every shot is deadly

options.how: Blackreef repeats one day split into morning, noon, afternoon and evening; targets move between districts by period, then it resets.
A school-year calendar split into daily time slots; each activity spends a slot, and Palaces must be cleared before dated deadlines.
The island never moves through a day or season, so light, shadows and sightlines used by puzzles stay constant.

sources.note: Deathloop: trapped in a timeloop on Blackreef, each loop a chance to change things
Persona 5: day periods and plot-driven deadlines across the school year
The Witness: island of puzzles

note: Persona 5 source is not on the allowed list and The Witness static time is unconfirmed

options.how: Four 30-day seasons decide which crops grow and which festivals happen; the farm is judged after a set number of years.

options.game: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time
options.how: Hyrule Field cycles from day to night; Stalchildren rise after dark, town gates close, and the Sun's Song skips ahead.

sources.note: Harvest Moon: seasons and calendar
Ocarina of Time: day and night cycle

note: Search budget ran out before these mechanics could be confirmed; check before marking verified

options.how: Floors sag and walls lean before they collapse, so teams open new routes through buildings and no two matches leave the same rubble.
Hand-designed lane maps keep their walls and cover; only a few scripted doors and drop walls change, so sites and angles stay learnable.

sources.note: The Finals: floors sag before they give way, walls lean before they fall, enhanced destruction in arenas
Valorant: traditional three-lane maps with fixed sites; Ascent bomb doors and Summit drop walls are the scripted exceptions

options.how: Four seasons with dated festivals (Spring Festival on Spring 17) and weekday events like the Saturday market set the rhythm of farm life.
No clock: courses have no time limit or passing day, so each Power Star mission waits until you jump into its painting.

sources.note: Fields of Mistria: changing seasons with new quests, festivals and villager outfits
Fields of Mistria: calendar of seasons, dated festivals and weekly events
Super Mario 64: no time limit within courses; Power Star missions reached through paintings
